tldr: Headlines across outlets uniformly frame the EU decision as a reversal of punishment against Russian oligarchs, with Ukrainian outrage the dominant advertised signal; a secondary cluster explicitly links the delisting to Azerbaijan's pardon of a French prisoner, making the transactional logic of the deal more visible at the headline layer than the EU internal political fractures that body texts elaborate.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The headline itself surfaces a documented hypocrisy: it names Volkov's criticism of the delisting and, in the same title, states he proposed lifting Fridman's sanctions himself years earlier — a contradiction legible before any body text is read.
RT's headline frames the EU delisting as institutional dishonesty ('won't admit') rather than a Kremlin win, distancing Russian state media from overtly celebrating the EU's fracture.

bottom_line: The headline layer simultaneously advertises Ukrainian outrage at an EU sanctions reversal and a France-Azerbaijan prisoner swap, making the deal's transactional logic visible upfront — whereas body texts dwelled on EU internal political fractures and Baltic isolation that headlines largely omit.
